skill.name: namekit
skill.description: Generate project names that match your naming convention, or check names you already have. Report lookup results separately for domains, npm packages, and GitHub account handles.
skill.summary: Rank project name ideas and check selected names across relevant namespaces.
skill.author: mimukit

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown formatting or harmless command references. The documented commands lack explicit argument safeguards and allow unverified RDAP redirects. The workflow can send unpublished names to search providers without separate approval and label namespaces as owned without verifying control.

remediation.issue: User and repository values enter shell command templates without explicit validation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate names, owners, and branch references for their intended use. Pass them as separate arguments and encode URL components instead of interpolating text into shell commands.

remediation.issue: Saving a naming note can inspect other worktrees and fetch from the configured remote.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose these operations before saving. Use the current worktree by default and ask before reading other worktrees or fetching.

remediation.issue: The RDAP lookup follows redirects without verifying the destination.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve the authoritative endpoint from trusted RDAP bootstrap data. Require HTTPS and verify the destination before following a redirect.

remediation.issue: Permission to probe a name does not clearly cover disclosure to web search providers.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users which services receive candidate names. Ask before web searches and let users keep unpublished candidates offline.

remediation.issue: The ownership exception relies on repository context rather than proof of control.
remediation.suggestion: Keep results as taken unless a namespace-specific source verifies the user's control. Do not use a repository owner as proof for unrelated services.

content.value_statement: A project name can fit your naming convention and still be taken where you need it. Namekit ranks candidates and reports lookup results for domains, npm packages, and GitHub account handles separately.
actual_capabilities: Use a supplied naming rule, infer one from examples, or inspect repository names when requested.
Rank 12 candidates by meaning, sound, how well word parts join, and ease of spelling.
Show the ranked shortlist before checking the two or three candidates the user selects.
Check existing names directly and report each namespace result without ranking or filtering.
Report failed or inconclusive lookups as unknown and identify skipped checks.
Search for existing products or possible trademark conflicts for the top available candidate.
limitations: Live checks depend on network access and tool availability. GitHub CLI requests can also require authentication.
A domain reported as unregistered may still be reserved, expensive, or unavailable for purchase.
A web search does not provide trademark clearance, and a yours label does not verify ownership.
The skill does not check social handles, register domains, publish packages, or create GitHub organizations.

use_cases.title: Check an npm Package Name
use_cases.description: Compare two package names in npm without generating alternatives or checking unrelated services.

use_cases.title: Shortlist Names for a New Product
use_cases.description: Rank names that fit an existing product family. Select finalists for domain and GitHub account checks.

use_cases.title: Name an Internal Tool
use_cases.description: Generate names that follow a team prefix. Skip external checks when the tool has no public namespace.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Existing Name
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Check a public package name.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether tabgrove is taken on npm only. Do not generate alternatives. Explain any unknown result.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Names Offline
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: Follow a specified naming convention.
prompt_templates.prompt: Name an internal build log viewer for developers. Use the prefix trace and a plain English tone. Show the ranked shortlist without external lookups.

prompt_templates.title: Infer a Naming Convention
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Match a family of public developer tools.
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest names for a command-line tool that compares configuration files. Infer our convention from loggrove and testgrove. Show the shortlist and let me pick names for domain and npm checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Checks for a Product Launch
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Limit which services receive candidate names.
prompt_templates.prompt: Name a release dashboard using our ship and trace themes. Use plain English and rank the shortlist. Ask before sending finalists to domain registries, GitHub, or web search. Keep the decision in this chat.

best_practices: Provide your naming convention or examples, target audience, and the services where the name will appear.
Check two or three finalists at a time and confirm which services may receive unpublished names.
Verify registration price, account control, and trademark status separately before choosing a name.
anti_patterns: Sending dozens of candidates at once can trigger rate limits and leave results unknown.
Treating a timeout, rate limit, or authentication error as proof of availability.
Assuming a GitHub account check confirms that a repository name is available within an organization.

faq.question: Which namespaces can Namekit check?
faq.answer: It checks domain registration, npm package names, and GitHub user or organization handles. It can skip services your project does not need.

faq.question: Can it generate names without internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a naming convention or examples. The skill can rank suggestions and report which live checks it skipped.

faq.question: What does an unknown result mean?
faq.answer: The lookup did not return a reliable answer. Rate limits, outages, missing authentication, or an unsupported domain suffix can cause this.

faq.question: Are unpublished names sent to external services?
faq.answer: Live checks send candidates to the relevant services. Generate mode also searches the selected finalist on the web. Request offline generation to keep names private.

faq.question: Does an unregistered domain mean the name is clear to use?
faq.answer: No. Registration status does not guarantee purchase availability or trademark clearance. Verify both separately before adopting the name.

faq.question: Does Namekit write files or claim names?
faq.answer: It writes a naming note only if requested in generate mode. It does not register domains, publish packages, or create GitHub organizations.
